title: Dengue deaths reach 474 as eight more die in a day
excerpt: DGHS recorded 1,595 admissions in the 24 hours to 8am on 10 November. Seven of the eight deaths were in Dhaka division.

image.alt: An Aedes aegypti mosquito, which spreads dengue, resting on a mosquito net

content:
Eight people died of dengue and 1,595 were admitted to hospital in the 24 hours to 8am on Tuesday, 10 November, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), The Daily Star reported.

The numbers

  • Deaths this year: 474. Seven of the latest deaths were in Dhaka division and one in Khulna division.
  • Admissions this year: 153,768.
  • In hospital now: 6,136, slightly more than the 6,114 reported a day earlier.
  • Trend: admissions fell from 2,260 on 9 November to 1,595, but deaths rose from five to eight. One day's figures can swing, so the weekly pattern is a better guide.

Why it matters

Deaths rose even as admissions fell, and most were in Dhaka division. With more than 6,000 people in hospital, health facilities are under steady pressure while the measles outbreak continues. NGOs with urban health, WASH and community volunteer programmes can help with breeding-site clean-ups and early referral, since late arrival at hospital is a common factor in dengue deaths.

What to watch

Whether the number of patients in hospital keeps rising this week, and whether deaths stay concentrated in Dhaka.
